description: Citation registry for the colour-analysis datasets. Every other dataset in data/ cites these by id rather than repeating a URL, so a source is described once and can be corrected in one place. `supports` states the specific claim the source is cited for — a citation that supports nothing is decoration. `botBlocked` marks pages a human can read in a browser but that reject automated readers; do not waste time re-testing them. Statuses were verified on 2026-07-29 with `make check-links`.

sources.title: WADA Sanzō (和田三造) — Dictionary of Artists in Japan
sources.publisher: Art Platform Japan, Agency for Cultural Affairs (go.jp)
sources.supports: The founding claim this whole design rests on, quoted exactly: 'In 1927 Wada established the Japan Standard Color Association (present-day Japan Color Research Institute)'. Also gives his dates, 1883-1967.

sources.title: Sanzo Wada
sources.supports: Wada biography and the 1933-34 publication dates of the colour-combination volumes reprinted as A Dictionary of Color Combinations.

sources.title: 日本色彩研究所 (Japan Color Research Institute)
sources.supports: The institute Wada founded, still operating. Publisher of PCCS.

sources.title: 沿革 (History) — Japan Color Research Institute
sources.supports: The institute's own account of its history. Note: the page renders its content with JavaScript, so an automated reader sees an empty document even though it returns 200 and reads normally in a browser.

sources.title: What is PCCS (Hue Circle, Tone Diagram)
sources.supports: PCCS was developed by the Japan Color Research Institute in 1964; the hue-tone structure; the twelve chromatic tone names and abbreviations with their impressions; construction of the 24-hue circle from four psychological primaries.

sources.title: PCCS
sources.supports: The 24 hues with Japanese and English names; the twelve chromatic and five achromatic tones; lightness running 1.5-9.5 in 0.5 steps and saturation 1s-9s. See the `notes` in pccs-tones.json for where this source is internally inconsistent.

sources.title: Korean Color Analysis (퍼스널컬러): Complete Guide for Western Readers
sources.supports: Korean personal-colour analysis reads undertone, depth and chroma, and is built on PCCS tones rather than on Western swatch books.

sources.title: Personal Color Analysis: The Korean Movement and the Western 12-Season Grid
sources.supports: The mapping of the four parent seasons onto sets of PCCS tones, and the distinction between Korean practice and the Western twelve-season grid.

sources.title: How Korean 12-Season Color Analysis Works
sources.supports: Korean studios subdivide the four seasons into eight or twelve types depending on the studio — evidence that the twelve-way split is not standardised, which is why ours is marked as ours.

sources.title: PCCS·KS 톤(light, bright, pale, soft)에 대한 색채 인식 비교 연구
sources.publisher: 한국디자인문화학회지 (Journal of the Korean Society of Design Culture), via DBpia
sources.supports: Peer-reviewed treatment of PCCS tones in a Korean personal-colour context, and evidence that tone boundaries are actively studied rather than settled.

sources.title: Munsell Color Science Lab Educational Resources — Munsell Renotation Data
sources.publisher: Rochester Institute of Technology, Munsell Color Science Laboratory
sources.supports: The Munsell renotation data (Newhall, Judd and Nickerson, JOSA, 1943), cited for the ancestry of the PCCS lightness scale: PCCS lightness is Munsell value. We do not vendor the data itself.

sources.title: The Sci\ART™ Personal Colour Analysis System
sources.supports: Kathryn Kalisz developed Sci\ART around 2000 while working at the Munsell Institute, framing the seasons in Munsell hue/value/chroma terms — the origin of the Western twelve-season vocabulary. Its bot detection is inconsistent: 200 to curl, 403 to fetch, on the same day. Reads normally in a browser.

sources.title: Sci\ART: A Brief Introduction
sources.supports: Independent account of the Sci\ART system and how the twelve-season vocabulary spread to other schools.

sources.title: Practical Color Coordinate System
sources.supports: PCCS tone groupings and the derivation of tones from the Munsell value and chroma scales. Readable in a browser; rejects automated readers.
